messages:
Alex K: Heads up — CI started failing on master after the attention-opt kernels landed. Build error looks like a mix of binary bloat + toolchain mismatch. Running out of artifact space and nvlink is failing intermittently.

Alex K: Error snippet: `ptxas info : Compiling entry function 'attn_kernel' for 'sm_86'
ptxas fatal : Unresolved global symbol '__device_stub__some_helper'
nvlink error : failed to generate cuda binary`

Maya R: ugh. Two things come to mind: (1) our fatbin contains cubins for ~8 arches which explodes size, (2) CI uses toolkit/driver combo that sometimes rejects newer PTX versions.

Maya R: Quick repro command I ran locally that reproduces the size and ptx noise:
```
nvcc -O3 -lineinfo -arch=sm_80 \
  -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 \
  -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 \
  -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 \
  -gencode=arch=compute_92,code=sm_92 \
  --fatbin -Xptxas=-v -o build/attn.fatbin src/attn.cu
```
This produces a ~180MB fatbin and ptxas prints newer PTX versions for sm_90/92. CI's CUDA 11.x runner chokes on those.

Chris L: Two practical mitigations: (A) stop bundling cubins for every arch in CI: only build host-targeted cubins for our supported matrix (sm_80, sm_86) and emit PTX for the rest, (B) split artifacts per-arch so CI caches smaller files. That keeps deployment flexible but reduces per-artifact size.

Chris L: Example per-arch split commands:
```
# generate arch-specific cubin
nvcc -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -cubin -o out/attn_sm80.cubin src/attn.cu
# generate PTX for forward compatibility
nvcc -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=compute_90 -ptx -o out/attn_compute90.ptx src/attn.cu
```
And in runtime we can load cubin if available, fallback to PTX JIT if driver supports it.

Maya R: Also try these flags to reduce size and keep register usage sane: `-maxrregcount=64 -Xptxas=-v -Xptxas=-O3` and only use `-use_fast_math` where safe. For relocatable device code we hit duplicate symbol/linker surprises; for that build with `-rdc=true` then `nvlink` separately.

Devon P: Agreed. My TODO: update the cmake/bazel rules so CI exposes BUILD_ARCH_LIST env var and we only produce cubins for BUILD_ARCH_LIST, and then produce PTX for a smaller compatibility list. I can open a PR to: (1) split fatbin targets, (2) add per-arch caching keys, (3) add a CI guard that fails if total artifact size > 120MB.

Devon P: Also note: older CI runners have CUDA 11.x and they interpret PTX versions differently. We should either: pin the CI toolkit to >=12.x (painful), or lower generated PTX by targeting older compute for the PTX outputs (i.e., `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=compute_80` for ptx generation).

Alex K: Sounds good. One extra gotcha: some of the attention microkernels use device-inlined helpers that get eliminated only with `-rdc=true` or proper NVCC visibility settings. That explains the unresolved externals for some builds. So the build split should ensure we compile related object files with the same `-rdc` setting when linking a fatbin.

Maya R: For quick CI stopgap we can: set BUILD_ARCH_LIST to `sm_80,sm_86`, change fatbin -> per-arch split, and add a sanity step that scans artifacts for PTX version strings and fails if > PTX 7.0 for CUDA11 runners. I'll post a patch. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Created ticket #DR-1234 "ci: reduce runtime kernel artifact size and PTX/toolkit mismatches" and attached current failing job logs.

Devon P: I'll open RFC follow-up/PR with the CMake changes and add docs on expected `nvcc` flags for contributors. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Chris L: Thanks — when PR is up ping #eng-runtime and I'll review the caching/CI side. :eyes:
